# LaNorme configuration for the guarded deep-agent service.
#
# A small FastAPI service, so no architecture profile: its modules (settings,
# guardrails, agent, chat service, routes, composition root in main.py) do not
# map onto hexagonal/clean/layered directories, and forcing that layout onto
# ~10 modules would add indirection without buying anything yet. Revisit when
# conversation memory adds a persistence adapter.

# Warnings (TYPE-004, NAMING-004, size and complexity warnings, advisories)
# fail the build too: the codebase is new, so there is no debt to grandfather.
promote = ["ALL"]

# Keyword-only parameters: call sites such as build_agent(model=..., tool_call_limit=...)
# stay readable and are robust to reordering.
[named_args]
enabled = true

# Public definitions of 5+ lines carry a docstring that says something.
[docstrings]
enabled = true

# Prefer direct attribute access / Protocols over hasattr/getattr with literals.
[attribute_access]
enabled = true

# Tests follow Given/When/Then and do not copy-paste setup. (Given/When/Then rather
# than Arrange/Act/Assert: '# Assert' above an assert line trips CMT-005 below.)
[test_style]
enabled = true

# Comments must add a why, not restate the code.
[restating]
enabled = true

# Flag structurally near-identical functions that should share a helper.
[similarity]
enabled = true

# No short variable names carried across a long span.
[naming_scope]
enabled = true

# Inline suppressions: zero budget, and any directive must name its rule.
[suppressions]
enabled = true

# No em dashes or emoji in comments/docstrings (house style).
[comments]
em_dash = true
emoji = true

# Left off deliberately:
# - naming_clean_code: its "every function starts with a verb" reading
#   conflicts with idiomatic Python names for value-returning functions.
# - prose: British vs American spelling is not a standard this project sets,
#   and there is no docs/ tree for the docs check to judge.

# LaNorme configuration for the guarded-agent service.
#
# Greenfield project, so start strict: the "strict" profile turns on every
# opt-in check and promotes all warnings to errors. There is no legacy code to
# baseline, and the codebase is small enough to keep fully clean.
extends = ["strict"]

# Layers live under app/ (domain, application, infrastructure, api). The
# built-in hexagonal layer_deps and port_coverage defaults (ports in
# application/ports, adapters in infrastructure/services) match this layout,
# so no architecture profile is needed. app/main.py is the composition root.
source_root = "app"

# Tests sit flat under tests/, not tests/integration.
[test_coverage]
test_roots = ["tests"]

# The one allowed inline suppression is AUTHN-001 on POST /chat: the HTTP
# contract fixes it as unauthenticated. Ratchet down if auth is added.
[suppressions]
max_total = 1

# No docs/ tree; README.md is the only Markdown, so the Diataxis check is moot.
[docs]
enabled = false

# Em dashes and emoji are kept out of comments and docstrings as well as Markdown.
[comments]
em_dash = true
emoji = true

# "reply" is the port's verb (the agent replies to a message).
[naming_clean_code]
verbs = ["reply"]

adapter_roots = ["infrastructure/services", "infrastructure/repositories"]

repo_crud = true

# LaNorme configuration for the guarded agent service.
#
# The project is new and small, so there is no legacy debt to excuse: adopt the
# bundled "strict" profile, which enables every opt-in check and promotes every
# advisory warning to a build-failing error. Starting strict is cheap now and
# much harder to retrofit later.
#
# What "strict" switches on, and why it suits this service:
#   named_args (KWARG-001)        guardrail and agent wiring passes several
#                                 knobs of the same type (ints, strings), so
#                                 keyword-only call sites stop silent mix-ups.
#   docstrings (CMT-006/007)      the guardrails are a contract other systems
#                                 rely on; public pieces should say what they
#                                 promise, not restate their signature.
#   test_style (AAA-001/002)      the tests double as the guardrail spec, so
#                                 they should read as arrange / act / assert.
#   restating, naming_scope,      cheap, precise readability checks.
#   naming_clean_code,
#   attribute_access, similarity
#   suppressions (budget 0)       a standard that one '# noqa' can waive is a
#                                 suggestion. Any exception must live here,
#                                 reviewed, not inline.
#   prose (PROSE-001..003)        README in British English, no em dashes or
#                                 emoji, matching the house style of the brief.
#   docs (DOCS-*)                 inert until a docs/ tree exists.
extends = ["strict"]

# Comments and docstrings follow the same prose rules as the README.
[comments]
em_dash = true
emoji = true

# Tests live in a flat tests/ directory rather than the default
# tests/integration layout.
[test_coverage]
test_roots = ["tests"]

# Not applicable here, deliberately left at their defaults:
#   layer_deps / port_coverage  the service is a handful of modules in one
#       package (config, guardrails, tools, agent, HTTP). Hexagonal layers would
#       be ceremony at this size; revisit if persistence or more adapters
#       arrive (conversation memory is planned).
#   AUTHN-001  the published contract has no authentication on /chat. If auth
#       is added, put routes under api/ so the rule starts enforcing it.

# The package is app/, so path-scoped rules (AUTHN-001 on api/, layer_deps,
# test_coverage) find its api/ directory relative to it.
source_root = "app"

# Comments and docstrings follow the same prose rules as the README.

em_dash = true
emoji = true

# Tests live in a flat tests/ directory rather than the default

# Routes live in app/api/, so AUTHN-001 enforces an auth dependency on every

# the tenant comes from X-Tenant-ID. Keep chat.py free of any other mutating
# route so this exemption covers nothing else.
[per-file-ignores]
"app/api/chat.py" = ["AUTHN-001"]

#       already sits behind the PolicyStore protocol in app/policies.py, which
#       is the seam a database needs; full hexagonal layers would be ceremony
#       at this size. Revisit when a real database or conversation memory
#       arrives.
